headline: My local tea shop owner has issued an ultimatum that I either buy his signature masala chai or he will drive my morning commute into hell
body:
I just wanted a quick cutting chai before heading to the office, but my local vendor, Ramesh, has turned my breakfast ritual into a high-stakes geopolitical standoff. As I reached for my wallet to pay the regular ten rupees, he slammed his ladle onto the counter and informed me that my patronage is now a binary choice between 'The Deal'—a monthly subscription for extra ginger—or the immediate atmospheric collapse of my commute.

He stood there, silhouetted against the steam of a giant aluminum pot, staring at me with the intensity of a head of state at the UN. 'It is a simple decision,' he told me, pointing a stained mixing spoon directly at my chest. 'You either subscribe to the premium ginger package today, or I will ensure your morning drive transforms into a personal, traffic-clogged hellscape that lasts until the end of the fiscal year.'

I’m not a diplomat, I’m an accountant, but I found myself sweating under the gaze of a man who clearly believes he has the power to manipulate the fabric of my reality through the medium of sweetened milk. I didn't want to risk the 'hell' part, so I signed the subscription form on the back of a crumpled napkin. I’m currently paying 500 rupees a month for a beverage that tastes identical to the one I used to get for ten, but at least my commute was light today.
caption: When the neighborhood chai point starts acting like the UN General Assembly, you know it's time to upgrade your subscription. Who knew the price of local peace was just a few extra slivers of ginger? #ChaiDiplomacy #OfficeLife #MorningCrisis (satire)
